title: Mayer-Vietoris sequence for etale cohomology
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $U,V\subseteq X$ be open subschemes with $X=U\cup V$; write $j_W:W\to X$ for the open immersion of an open $W\in\{U,V,U\cap V\}$. Let $F$ be an abelian sheaf on the small etale site $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], and write $F|_W=j_W^{-1}F$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] (for an open immersion this is the restriction $F|_W(T)=F(T)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction]). Then there is a long exact sequence of abelian groups, functorial in $F$,
$$
0\to H^0(X_{\Et},F)\to H^0(U_{\Et},F|_U)\oplus H^0(V_{\Et},F|_V)\to H^0((U\cap V)_{\Et},F|_{U\cap V})\to H^1(X_{\Et},F)\to\cdots
$$
$$
\cdots\to H^{q-1}((U\cap V)_{\Et},F|_{U\cap V})\xrightarrow{\ \delta\ }H^q(X_{\Et},F)\xrightarrow{(\rho_U,\rho_V)}H^q(U_{\Et},F|_U)\oplus H^q(V_{\Et},F|_V)\xrightarrow{\rho-\rho}H^q((U\cap V)_{\Et},F|_{U\cap V})\xrightarrow{\ \delta\ }H^{q+1}(X_{\Et},F)\to\cdots,
$$
where $H^q$ is etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] and the maps $\rho$ are the restriction (pullback) maps along the open immersions. In particular, if $H^q(U_{\Et},F|_U)=H^q(V_{\Et},F|_V)=0$ and $H^{q-1}((U\cap V)_{\Et},F|_{U\cap V})=0$, then $H^q(X_{\Et},F)=0$. (Stacks states the sequence with $H^q_{\Et}(W,F)$, the derived functors of $G\mapsto G(W)$ on $\Ab(X_{\Et})$; these are identified with $H^q(W_{\Et},F|_W)$ by Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 03F3 (2) (sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-cohomology-of-open), which is part of this statement.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A50 (lemma-mayer-vietoris), with Cohomology on Sites Lemma Tag 03F3 (sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-cohomology-of-open) for the identification $H^q_{\Et}(W,F)=H^q(W_{\Et},F|_W)$

proof.text: *The covering and its fibre products.* The open immersions $j_U:U\to X$, $j_V:V\to X$, $j_{U\cap V}:U\cap V\to X$ and the inclusions $k_U:U\cap V\to U$, $k_V:U\cap V\to V$ are etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (1), so $X,U,V,U\cap V$ are objects of $X_{\Et}$ and the inclusions are morphisms of $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Since $X=U\cup V$, the family $\mathcal U=\{U\to X,V\to X\}$ is jointly surjective, hence a covering of $X$ in $X_{\Et}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] (with $S=X$, both maps $\mathrm{id}_X$, and the opens $U,V$ resp. $U,U$, etc.), every fibre product $W_0\times_XW_1\times_X\cdots\times_XW_p$ with $W_k\in\{U,V\}$ is identified with the open subscheme $W_0\cap\cdots\cap W_p$, the projections becoming the inclusions; in particular $U\times_XU=U$, $V\times_XV=V$ (both projections the identity), $U\times_XV=V\times_XU=U\cap V$, and every product containing both $U$ and $V$ is $U\cap V$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A50 (lemma-mayer-vietoris), proof: 'the covering X = U ∪ V'

proof.text: *Sections of an abelian sheaf: left exactness.* Let $\mathcal I$ be an abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ and consider $0\to\mathcal I(X)\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal I(U)\oplus\mathcal I(V)\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal I(U\cap V)$ with $a(s)=(s|_U,s|_V)$ and $b(s,t)=s|_{U\cap V}-t|_{U\cap V}$; $b\circ a=0$ since restriction is functorial. The sheaf condition [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] for the covering $\mathcal U$ of step 1 says $\mathcal I(X)\to\mathcal I(U)\times\mathcal I(V)\rightrightarrows\prod_{W,W'\in\{U,V\}}\mathcal I(W\times_XW')$ is an equalizer. By step 1 the two components on $U\times_XU=U$ and on $V\times_XV=V$ of the two arrows agree for every $(s,t)$ (both projections are the identity), and those on $U\times_XV$ and $V\times_XU$ both say $s|_{U\cap V}=t|_{U\cap V}$. So $a$ is injective, and $(s,t)$ with $b(s,t)=0$ is $a$ of a (unique) section: the sequence is exact at $\mathcal I(X)$ and at $\mathcal I(U)\oplus\mathcal I(V)$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A50, proof: 'This is true in the first and middle spots as I is a sheaf'

proof.text: *Surjectivity on the right for an injective sheaf.* Let $\mathcal I$ be an injective object of $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions] and $\gamma\in\mathcal I(U\cap V)$. Index $\mathcal U$ by $\{U,V\}$ and use the identifications of step 1. Define $c\in\check{\mathcal C}^1(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)=\prod_{(i,j)}\mathcal I(U_i\times_XU_j)$ [def-weil-pbc-cech-complex] by $c_{UU}=0$, $c_{VV}=0$, $c_{UV}=\gamma$, $c_{VU}=-\gamma$; i.e. $c_{ij}=(\varphi(j)-\varphi(i))\gamma$ with $\varphi(U)=0,\varphi(V)=1$, where $\gamma$ stands for its restriction to $U_i\times_XU_j$ whenever $i\neq j$. $c$ is a cocycle: $d(c)_{i_0i_1i_2}=c_{i_1i_2}-c_{i_0i_2}+c_{i_0i_1}$ restricted to $U_{i_0}\times_XU_{i_1}\times_XU_{i_2}$; if $i_0=i_1=i_2$ all three terms are $0$; otherwise the triple product is $U\cap V$, all three terms are multiples of $\gamma|_{U\cap V}=\gamma$ (restrictions along the projections being the identity of $U\cap V$ or the inclusions, by step 1), and the coefficient is $(\varphi(i_2)-\varphi(i_1))-(\varphi(i_2)-\varphi(i_0))+(\varphi(i_1)-\varphi(i_0))=0$. Since $\mathcal I$ is injective, $\check H^1(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)=0$ [lem-weil-pbc-injective-sheaf-cech-acyclic], so $c=d(\sigma)$ for some $\sigma=(\sigma_U,\sigma_V)\in\check{\mathcal C}^0=\mathcal I(U)\times\mathcal I(V)$, i.e. $c_{ij}=\sigma_j|-\sigma_i|$. For $(i,j)=(U,V)$: $\gamma=\sigma_V|_{U\cap V}-\sigma_U|_{U\cap V}=b(-\sigma_U,-\sigma_V)$. Hence $b$ is surjective, and with step 2, $0\to\mathcal I(X)\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal I(U)\oplus\mathcal I(V)\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal I(U\cap V)\to0$ is exact. (This is Stacks' second argument; its first argument, Cohomology on Sites Lemma 093X, surjectivity of $\mathcal I(U)\to\mathcal I(U\cap V)$ along the monomorphism $k_U$, would need a node of its own and is not used.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A50, proof: 'Another way to prove it would be to show that the cokernel of the map I(U) ⊕ I(V) → I(U ∩ V) is the first Čech cohomology group of I with respect to the covering X = U ∪ V which vanishes by Lemmas 03OR (lemma-hom-injective) and 03OV (lemma-forget-injectives)'

proof.text: *The short exact sequence of complexes.* $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ has enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives], so $F$ has an injective resolution $s:F\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ with $\mathcal I^n=0$ for $n<0$ [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] (1); it is a K-injective resolution, a bounded below complex of injectives being K-injective [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] (2), so $H^q(X_{\Et},F)=\mathcal H^q(\mathcal I^\bullet(X))$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Applying steps 2-3 to each $\mathcal I^n$ gives, degreewise, short exact sequences $0\to\mathcal I^n(X)\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal I^n(U)\oplus\mathcal I^n(V)\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal I^n(U\cap V)\to0$; $a$ and $b$ commute with the differentials, the differentials $\mathcal I^n\to\mathcal I^{n+1}$ being morphisms of sheaves and so commuting with restriction. So $0\to\mathcal I^\bullet(X)\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal I^\bullet(U)\oplus\mathcal I^\bullet(V)\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal I^\bullet(U\cap V)\to0$ is a sequence of complexes of abelian groups, short exact in each degree, and $\mathcal H^q$ of the middle complex is $\mathcal H^q(\mathcal I^\bullet(U))\oplus\mathcal H^q(\mathcal I^\bullet(V))$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A50, proof: 'Thus, if F → I^• is an injective resolution, then 0 → I^•(X) → I^•(U) ⊕ I^•(V) → I^•(U ∩ V) → 0 is a short exact sequence of complexes'

proof.text: *The long exact sequence.* By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] (in the abelian category of abelian groups) the sequence of step 4 has connecting maps $\delta^q:\mathcal H^q(\mathcal I^\bullet(U\cap V))\to\mathcal H^{q+1}(\mathcal I^\bullet(X))$ with $\cdots\to\mathcal H^q(\mathcal I^\bullet(X))\xrightarrow{\mathcal H^q(a)}\mathcal H^q(\mathcal I^\bullet(U))\oplus\mathcal H^q(\mathcal I^\bullet(V))\xrightarrow{\mathcal H^q(b)}\mathcal H^q(\mathcal I^\bullet(U\cap V))\xrightarrow{\delta^q}\mathcal H^{q+1}(\mathcal I^\bullet(X))\to\cdots$ exact; since all complexes vanish in negative degrees, $\mathcal H^{-1}=0$ and the sequence starts with $0\to\mathcal H^0(\mathcal I^\bullet(X))$. $\mathcal H^q(a)=(\mathcal H^q(r_U),\mathcal H^q(r_V))$ and $\mathcal H^q(b)=\mathcal H^q(r'_U)-\mathcal H^q(r'_V)$, where $r_W:\mathcal I^\bullet(X)\to\mathcal I^\bullet(W)$, $r'_W:\mathcal I^\bullet(W)\to\mathcal I^\bullet(U\cap V)$ are the restriction maps of complexes.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A50, proof: 'the associated long exact cohomology sequence is the sequence of the statement'; homology.tex Lemma Tag 0117

proof.text: *Identification of the terms and of the maps (Stacks 03F3 (2) and the pullback maps).* For $W\in\{U,V,U\cap V\}$, $j_W$ is etale (step 1). By [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] clause 5 (whose proof uses that restriction along an etale map preserves injectives), $j_W^{-1}F\to j_W^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet$ is a resolution of $F|_W=j_W^{-1}F$ by a bounded below complex of injective abelian sheaves on $W_{\Et}$, hence $H^q(W_{\Et},F|_W)=\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(W,j_W^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet))$, and $\rho_{\mathcal I^\bullet}(W):\Gamma(W,j_W^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal I^\bullet(W)$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (1), an isomorphism of complexes by naturality of $\rho$, identifies $H^q(W_{\Et},F|_W)\cong\mathcal H^q(\mathcal I^\bullet(W))$ (this is Stacks 03F3 (2) for $X_{\Et}/W=W_{\Et}$); for $W=X$ this is the definition. Under these identifications: (i) the pullback $j_W^*:H^q(X_{\Et},F)\to H^q(W_{\Et},F|_W)$ [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] is $\mathcal H^q(r_W)$, by the same clause 5 ($J^\bullet=j_W^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet$, $r=\mathrm{id}$; $u^*$ is $\mathcal H^q$ of the restriction $\mathcal I^\bullet(X)\to\mathcal I^\bullet(W)$ through $\rho$). (ii) For $k=k_U:U\cap V\to U$ (likewise $k_V$), the restriction map $\rho$ of the statement is $H^q(c_{j_U,k,F})\circ k^*:H^q(U_{\Et},F|_U)\to H^q((U\cap V)_{\Et},k^{-1}j_U^{-1}F)\to H^q((U\cap V)_{\Et},F|_{U\cap V})$, with $c_{j_U,k}:k^{-1}j_U^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{U\cap V}^{-1}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]. Clause 5 applied to $k$ and $G=j_U^{-1}F$ with its injective resolution $j_U^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet$ gives $k^*=\mathcal H^q$ of the restriction $\Gamma(U,j_U^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet)\to\Gamma(U\cap V,j_U^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet)$ of the sheaf $j_U^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet$ along $k$, which under $\rho_{\mathcal I^\bullet}$ (natural in the object of $U_{\Et}$) is $r'_U:\mathcal I^\bullet(U)\to\mathcal I^\bullet(U\cap V)$; and $H^q(c_{j_U,k,F})$ is computed by the isomorphism of complexes $c_{j_U,k,\mathcal I^\bullet}$ (a lift of $c_{j_U,k,F}$ between the two injective resolutions $k^{-1}j_U^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet$ and $j_{U\cap V}^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet$, natural in the sheaf) which under the identifications $\rho$ with $\mathcal I^\bullet(U\cap V)$ is the identity: both $\rho_{j_U^{-1}\mathcal I}\circ k^{-1}(\rho_{\mathcal I})$-type identifications and $\rho_{\mathcal I}\circ c$ are isomorphisms $k^{-1}j_U^{-1}\mathcal I\to\mathcal I|_{U\cap V}$ whose composite with the unit $\eta_{j_U\circ k}$ (via the unit compatibility of $c$ in [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]) is the restriction $\mathcal I(T)\to\mathcal I(T\times_X(U\cap V))$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (2), so they agree by uniqueness of the adjoint transpose. Hence under the identifications the maps of the statement are $(\rho_U,\rho_V)=\mathcal H^q(a)$ and $\rho-\rho=\mathcal H^q(b)$, and $\delta:=\delta^{q}$ transported; with step 5 this is the long exact sequence of the statement.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03F3 (lemma-cohomology-of-open), proof: 'F|_U → I^•|_U is an injective resolution in Mod(O_U). Hence H^p(U, F|_U) is equal to H^p(I^•|_U(U))'; etale-cohomology.tex Lemma Tag 0A50

proof.text: *Independence and functoriality in $F$.* Let $\varphi:F\to F'$ be a morphism of abelian sheaves on $X_{\Et}$ and $F'\to\mathcal I'^\bullet$ an injective resolution as in step 4. By [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] there is a morphism of complexes $\tilde\varphi:\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal I'^\bullet$ lifting $\varphi$ up to homotopy, and $H^q(\varphi)$ on $H^q(T_{\Et},-)$ is $\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(T,\tilde\varphi))$, independent of $\tilde\varphi$; for $W\in\{U,V,U\cap V\}$, $j_W^{-1}\tilde\varphi$ lifts $j_W^{-1}\varphi$, so under the identifications of step 6 $H^q(j_W^{-1}\varphi)$ is $\mathcal H^q(\tilde\varphi(W))$. Since restriction is natural for the sheaf morphisms $\tilde\varphi^n$, $(\tilde\varphi(X),\tilde\varphi(U)\oplus\tilde\varphi(V),\tilde\varphi(U\cap V))$ is a morphism from the short exact sequence of complexes of step 4 for $F$ to that for $F'$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality] the maps $H^q(\varphi)$, $H^q(\varphi|_U)\oplus H^q(\varphi|_V)$, $H^q(\varphi|_{U\cap V})$ form a morphism of long exact sequences (the connecting maps commute with them). With $\varphi=\mathrm{id}_F$ and two choices of resolution, this shows that the sequence (in particular $\delta$) does not depend on the injective resolution, up to the canonical identifications $H^q(\mathrm{id})$ [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial]; so the sequence is well defined and functorial in $F$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A50, statement: 'This long exact sequence is functorial in F' (not proved in the source; written out here); homology.tex Lemma Tag 0117 ('functorial in the short exact sequence')

proof.text: *The vanishing consequence.* If $H^q(U_{\Et},F|_U)=H^q(V_{\Et},F|_V)=0$ and $H^{q-1}((U\cap V)_{\Et},F|_{U\cap V})=0$, exactness of $H^{q-1}((U\cap V)_{\Et},F|_{U\cap V})\xrightarrow{\delta}H^q(X_{\Et},F)\xrightarrow{(\rho_U,\rho_V)}H^q(U_{\Et},F|_U)\oplus H^q(V_{\Et},F|_V)$ (steps 5-6; for $q=0$ the left term is $0$) gives $H^q(X_{\Et},F)=0$.
